- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average of history, adjust forecast toward historical mean (not latest peak or trough).
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), model tends to oscillate; use sentiment-weighted average (e.g., 60% recent, 40% 14-day avg) for smoothing.
